plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MSFU, PLTU, MUU) to zero for capital preservation.
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single-name concentration limit.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk.
It aims for a large cash buffer by exiting high-risk positions.
conservative.read: This conservative approach targets around 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces drawdown risk by eliminating leveraged positions and maintaining a cash buffer.

plan: Trim all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, MSFU, PLTU, MUU) to small, manageable positions.
Reduce QQQI to 25% to comply with the single-name concentration limit.
Buy SOXS at 4% as a strong scanner long setup to add targeted exposure.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a small cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced approach aims for approximately 2.5% per month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage while introducing a high-quality scanner long setup, maintaining moderate drawdown potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single-name concentration limit.
Add to existing leveraged ETFs (METU, MSFU, SOXL, PLTU, MUU, SPAL) to increase growth potential.
Buy SOXS at 6% as a high-scoring scanner long setup.
This plan leans into leverage and concentration for aggressive growth.
It maintains a smaller cash buffer and wider stops.
aggressive.read: This aggressive growth approach targets around 4% per month, stretching for higher returns. It significantly increases both upside potential and drawdown risk due to amplified leverage and daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and high-beta single names (METU, MSFU, PLTU, MUU) to zero.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced income.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
It aims to park cash for yield, reducing growth-oriented exposure.
income.read: This income-focused approach targets around 1% per month, prioritizing reliable distributions. It significantly reduces growth and drawdown risk by cutting leveraged and high-beta positions. Distributions are variable, and NAV can still decline in market downturns.
